name: Expired Pointer Dereference
principle: Code dereferences a pointer to memory that was once valid but has expired after free, scope exit, or release. The stale address may now refer to inaccessible memory or attacker-influenced reused storage, causing crash, data exposure, corruption, or code execution.
detection_signals: pointer passed to function, read, write, delete, or free after free(ptr)
pointer dereferenced after delete ptr or delete[] ptr
field/global pointer freed in one branch and later used without reassignment
same pointer freed twice on multiple control-flow paths
address of local stack variable returned or stored beyond its scope
container/object stores raw pointer to object whose owner calls free/delete
callback/function pointer invoked after associated object memory was freed
negative_signals: ptr is set to NULL/nullptr immediately after free/delete and checked before use
ownership transferred with std::unique_ptr or std::shared_ptr instead of raw pointer
all uses occur before the only free/delete on every control-flow path
pointer is reassigned to a fresh malloc/new result before later dereference
C++ RAII object lifetime encloses every dereference and no raw escaping pointer exists
false_defense_traps: setting only one alias to NULL while other aliases still point to freed memory
checking ptr != NULL after free when the pointer was not nulled
assuming malloc reuse will not occur before stale pointer use
freeing in an error path and logging with the same pointer later
manual comments about ownership without enforced single owner
verification_focus: Can any dereference, read/write, function call, or second release occur after the pointed-to storage has expired on any control-flow path?

consequence_chains.trigger: caller dereferences an address returned for a local stack variable after the callee returns
stale pointer is used for a read after the allocation is gone or size metadata is no longer valid
consequence_chains.consequence: out-of-bounds read and information exposure or crash

consequence_chains.trigger: stale pointer is used for a write after the memory is reallocated or invalid
consequence_chains.consequence: out-of-bounds write, heap corruption, or code execution

patch_principle: Use automatic memory management or RAII ownership where possible.
Establish a single clear owner for each allocation and release it once.
Set freed raw pointers to NULL/nullptr and invalidate all aliases when feasible.
Move logging, cleanup, and reads before free/delete, or copy needed data before release.
Prefer smart pointers and containers over raw malloc/free or new/delete.
